questions.subject: Karnataka Art and Heritage

options.A: Virupaksha Temple at Pattadakal – Queen Lokamahadevi
options.B: Chennakeshava Temple at Belur – Vishnuvardhana
options.C: Keshava Temple at Somanathapura – Somanatha Dandanayaka
options.D: Hoysaleswara Temple at Halebidu – Krishnaraja Wadiyar III

questions.explanation: The Hoysaleswara Temple at Halebidu is a major Hoysala temple dedicated to Shiva, renowned for intricate soapstone sculpture. It is not associated with Krishnaraja Wadiyar III, who patronised Mysore painting.

questions.subject: Karnataka Art and Heritage
questions.topic: UNESCO World Heritage and Related Heritage Sites
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Karnataka's UNESCO World Heritage properties is correct?

options.A: Hampi, Pattadakal and Badami are all inscribed World Heritage Sites
options.B: Hampi was inscribed in 1986, Pattadakal in 1987 and the Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas in 2023
options.C: Aihole is an inscribed World Heritage Site
options.D: The Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas were inscribed in 1986

questions.explanation: As of 2026, Karnataka has three inscribed cultural World Heritage properties: Hampi (1986), Pattadakal (1987) and the Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas (2023). Badami and Aihole are on the Tentative List, not inscribed.

questions.subject: Karnataka Art and Heritage
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the components of Yakshagana?

options.A: Himmela refers to actors and Mummela refers to musicians
options.B: Himmela refers to the musical ensemble and Mummela refers to the actors and dancers
options.C: Both Himmela and Mummela refer to musicians
options.D: Both Himmela and Mummela refer to actors

questions.explanation: In Yakshagana, Himmela is the musical ensemble of singers and instrumentalists accompanying the performance, while Mummela refers to the actors and dancers who enact the dramatic story.

questions.subject: Karnataka Art and Heritage
questions.question: Match the folk dance with its description: (i) Dollu Kunitha (ii) Veeragase (iii) Kamsale (iv) Huli Vesha

options.A: (i) Drum dance, (ii) Shaivite dance of Veerabhadra, (iii) Devotional dance with metal instruments, (iv) Tiger-costume dance
options.B: (i) Tiger-costume dance, (ii) Drum dance, (iii) Shaivite dance, (iv) Devotional dance
options.C: (i) Devotional dance, (ii) Tiger-costume dance, (iii) Drum dance, (iv) Shaivite dance
options.D: (i) Shaivite dance, (ii) Devotional dance, (iii) Tiger-costume dance, (iv) Drum dance

questions.explanation: Dollu Kunitha is a vigorous group dance performed to the beat of large drums called dollu; Veeragase is a Shaivite folk dance associated with Veerabhadra and the Dakshayajna narrative; Kamsale is a devotional dance using paired metal instruments associated with Male Mahadeshwara worship; Huli Vesha is a tiger-costume dance tradition popular in coastal Karnataka during festivals.

questions.subject: Karnataka Art and Heritage
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Bidriware is NOT correct?

options.A: It is a metal inlay craft known for silver designs on a dark, oxidised alloy surface
options.B: A zinc-dominant alloy containing copper is used as the base metal, with silver inlay
options.C: The dark background is created by treating the alloy surface with soil associated with the Bidar region
options.D: It is named after a Hoysala king who patronised the craft

questions.explanation: Bidriware is named after Bidar, where the craft developed and became strongly established. It was patronised by the Bahmani rulers and later Deccan courts, not by a Hoysala king.

questions.subject: Karnataka Art and Heritage
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Gommateshwara statue is correct?

options.A: It is a monolithic statue of Bahubali at Shravanabelagola, consecrated in 981 CE by Chavundaraya
options.B: It is a statue of Mahavira at Karkala, consecrated in 1432 CE
options.C: It is a bronze statue at Venur, erected in 1604 CE
options.D: It is a statue of Buddha at Sarnath

questions.explanation: The Gommateshwara statue is a monumental monolithic statue of Bahubali at Shravanabelagola in Hassan district, commissioned by Chavundaraya and consecrated in 981 CE.

questions.subject: Karnataka Art and Heritage
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Hampi is NOT correct?

options.A: It was the historic capital region of the Vijayanagara Empire
options.B: The Virupaksha Temple at Hampi is dedicated to Shiva
options.C: The Vittala Temple at Hampi is famous for its Stone Chariot and musical pillars
options.D: The Hoysaleswara Temple is located at Hampi

questions.explanation: The Hoysaleswara Temple is located at Halebidu in Hassan district, not at Hampi. Hampi's major monuments include the Virupaksha Temple, Vittala Temple, Hazara Rama Temple, Lotus Mahal and Elephant Stables.

questions.subject: Karnataka Art and Heritage
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Purandara Dasa is correct?

options.A: He is traditionally called the father of Carnatic music and is credited with systematising basic lessons such as sarali varsi, jantai varsi and alankaras
options.B: He was a Hindustani vocalist of the Kirana gharana
options.D: He was a veena player of the Mysore court

questions.explanation: Purandara Dasa is traditionally called the father of Carnatic music because of his foundational contribution to music pedagogy and devotional composition. He is credited with systematising basic lessons such as sarali varsi, jantai varsi and alankaras and composing many devotional songs.

questions.subject: Karnataka Art and Heritage

options.A: Yakshagana is a UNESCO World Heritage Site
options.B: Mysore painting is a UNESCO World Heritage Site
options.C: Badami and Aihole are on India's Tentative List but are not among Karnataka's three inscribed World Heritage properties
options.D: Karnataka has five inscribed World Heritage properties as of 2026

questions.explanation: Badami and Aihole are important heritage sites and have been included in India's Tentative List, but they are not among Karnataka's three inscribed World Heritage properties. Yakshagana and Mysore painting are important cultural traditions but should not be described as UNESCO World Heritage Sites unless formally inscribed.

options.A: It is the traditional art of hand-painted playing cards, historically associated with Persian origins and developed in distinctive forms under Indian royal patronage
options.B: It is a type of mural painting

questions.subject: Karnataka Art and Heritage
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Gol Gumbaz is correct?

options.A: It is the mausoleum of Adil Shah ruler Muhammad Adil Shah at Vijayapura, famous for its enormous dome and whispering gallery
options.B: It is the mausoleum of Tipu Sultan at Srirangapatna
options.C: It is a Hoysala temple at Halebidu
options.D: It is a palace in Mysuru

questions.explanation: Gol Gumbaz is the mausoleum of Adil Shah ruler Muhammad Adil Shah at Vijayapura, famous for its enormous dome and whispering gallery. The Whispering Gallery is the gallery around the interior of the dome where faint sounds can travel and be heard across the space due to acoustic reflection.

options.C: It is an Indian law passed in 1958

questions.subject: Karnataka Art and Heritage
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Mysore Palace is correct?

options.A: It was rebuilt in the Indo-Saracenic style after the earlier palace was destroyed by fire in 1897 and was designed by Henry Irwin
options.B: It was built by Tipu Sultan in the 18th century
options.C: It was designed by E. W. Fritchley in 1921

questions.explanation: The Mysore Palace is the royal palace of the Wadiyar dynasty in Mysuru, rebuilt in the Indo-Saracenic style after the earlier palace was destroyed by fire in 1897. British architect Henry Irwin designed the present palace, completed in the early 20th century and inaugurated in 1912.

questions.subject: Karnataka Art and Heritage
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Hoysala sculpture is correct?

options.A: It is especially known for intricate soapstone carving, detailed ornamentation, narrative friezes and finely modelled figures
options.B: It primarily uses granite and is known for simple unadorned surfaces
options.C: It is exclusively found in Badami cave temples
options.D: It is a form of bronze casting

questions.explanation: Hoysala sculpture is especially known for intricate soapstone carving, detailed ornamentation, narrative friezes, finely modelled figures and highly decorative temple surfaces. Soapstone's workable softness when quarried allowed detailed carving, and it hardens over time after exposure.

options.C: Sannata – a type of puppetry from coastal Karnataka
options.D: Krishna Parijata – a Jain religious text

questions.subject: Karnataka Art and Heritage

options.B: Badami is a Hoysala temple town
options.C: Badami is a Jain pilgrimage centre with the Gommateshwara statue
options.D: Badami is a UNESCO World Heritage Site

questions.explanation: Badami was the capital of the Early Chalukyas and is known for rock-cut cave temples, structural temples and the Badami fort complex. Four major rock-cut cave temples are commonly identified, representing Hindu, Jain and other religious iconographic traditions. The Bhutanatha temple group is a group of sandstone temples near the Agastya Lake at Badami, associated with Shiva worship. Badami is on India's Tentative List but is not an inscribed UNESCO World Heritage Site.
